guides.109gyii3c8x: **Narita (NRT)** is far from the city; the connection to the centre takes about an hour by express train and longer by bus, depending on traffic. On flights landing late at night, check the last train time in advance — if you miss it, a taxi fare in Japan is a serious sum.
guides.109hu654ie: If you're looking for architecture and wide open space, **Moerenuma Park**, designed by Isamu Noguchi, needs half a day; it shouldn't be squeezed into a walk around the centre. In winter, facilities and transport may differ from summer. The Sapporo Beer Museum tells the city's beer history through red-brick industrial heritage. Since 1 July 2026, old "completely free museum" information no longer applies: self-guided entry has been announced at ¥1,000 for adults and a guided tour with two tastings at ¥2,000. Check advance sales and current conditions on the official site.

guides.10iinwipogu: Los Angeles isn't as simple as "you can't see it without a car". The Metro rail system connects Downtown, Koreatown, Hollywood, Santa Monica, Pasadena and the surrounding area; the bus network is wider. If your hotel and main sights are on these lines, spending the first two days without a car is possible. If you're planning Malibu, mountain hikes, lots of far-flung food stops or the studio area, a car starts to make sense.
guides.10me206dgb1: **Long Island City** and **Downtown Brooklyn**, if close to the right subway station, are fast options despite being outside Manhattan. The key question here isn't "how many kilometres to Manhattan?" but which line you can board from the hotel without changing. A cheap hotel in New Jersey, meanwhile, can claw back the savings you expect in time, because of PATH or bus frequency, late-night returns and a separate fare system.

guides.10n5idtf7ij: In the city, 500 metres isn't always a five-minute walk. The pavement may end, a junction may need a footbridge, and the midday heat slows your pace.
